_maintainer_note: The curated list of online knowledge sources the setup wizard is allowed to fetch. This file IS the allowlist: puffpai.source_fetch will not download from any address that is not spelled out here, so adding a row is granting a network permission, not filing a bookmark. Rules, so this stays safe as sources rotate: (1) LICENSE IS MANDATORY. A row with no 'license' is never offered and never fetched - the loader drops it and records a config-health defect naming the id. Put the SPDX-ish id in 'license' and the page you read it on in 'license_url', and actually read that page before you add the row; record the date you read it, or true, in 'license_checked'. A row whose license could not be confirmed says 'license_checked': false, names the best-known terms in 'license', and carries 'commercial_use': false until someone confirms otherwise. (2) NC MEANS NC. Rows marked with a NonCommercial license are fine for a person's own bot and are NOT fine to redistribute in a commercial bundle; they carry 'commercial_use': false and the wizard says so out loud. (3) HTTPS ONLY, DEFAULT PORT, NO USERINFO. A row that needs anything else does not go in. (4) REDIRECTS STAY HOME. A download may only follow redirects to the row's own host unless 'redirect_hosts' names the mirrors, and every hop is re-checked against the private-address rules. Name mirrors explicitly; do not open a wildcard. (4b) EVERY ROW WITH A URL MAKES AN EXPLICIT INTEGRITY CLAIM. There is no silence here: a row carries either a real 'sha256' the maintainer measured, or 'pin': 'none' with a 'pin_reason' saying in words why it cannot carry one. a row that does neither does not go in, and a 'corpus' row may NOT use 'pin': 'none' at all - a corpus row names one fixed file, so it MUST pin. A 'corpus' row names one fixed file, so it MUST carry a 'sha256'; a corpus row without one does not go in. The digest is verified after download and a mismatch is a hard stop with the file set aside - it is the only thing standing between this wizard and a listed host that has been compromised or has quietly swapped a file. 'zim' and 'docs' rows are the two kinds that cannot carry one honestly, and they say so per row rather than being exempted by a rule nobody can see: 'zim' rows point at a library that reissues its files under the same URL on its own schedule (all the Kiwix rows), and 'docs' rows point at a landing page rather than a download. BE HONEST ABOUT WHAT THAT COSTS: every row in this file today is 'pin': 'none', which means nothing downloaded through this registry is currently verified against a digest. The Kiwix library publishes a sibling .sha256 next to each ZIM and fetching that at download time is the real fix; it is an open follow-up, not a solved problem, and nobody should read this file as though the downloads were pinned. A digest you did not measure yourself is worse than none, so leave it out rather than guess - and if you cannot measure it, the row does not belong here. MUTABLE REFS ARE NOT SOURCES: a URL that resolves through a moving branch name (a GitHub '/main/', a '/latest/' redirect) can serve different bytes tomorrow and therefore cannot be pinned at all. Name an immutable tag or commit and pin its digest, or leave it out. This is why the HYG star database is not listed: its natural URL is raw.githubusercontent.com/astronexus/HYG-Database/main/... with no digest, so anyone who could push to that branch could land 35 MB of anything of their choosing on an owner's machine, and this file - which IS the allowlist - would be granting that. Add it by pinning a tag or commit SHA in the URL and recording a sha256 the maintainer measured. The provenance record says 'sha256_pinned': false when it was measured but not checked, which is what an auditor needs to know. (5) size_mb IS APPROXIMATE and is there so a person is never surprised - the fetcher shows the server's real Content-Length before a byte lands, and refuses a body that runs past the ceiling derived from this number. Keep it roughly right; a wildly low number becomes a refused download, not a silent 50 GB. (6) TAGS ARE THE MATCHING SURFACE. A source is only ever proposed when a specific tag or a word from our own label appears in what the person typed, and the proposal cites that term. Tags that are function words can never match, so do not add them. (7) FETCHED CONTENT IS DATA, FOREVER. Nothing downloaded through this registry is ever placed in a prompt as instruction, no matter what it says about itself. (7b) KIWIX ROWS USE THE UNDATED NAME. Kiwix file names carry a date, and https://download.kiwix.org/zim/<name>.zim (no folder, no date) redirects to the newest dated file, so 'source_url' and 'filename' use the undated name. 'known_good' names one dated file that is known to open in our reader. (8) Kiwix ZIM files are read by our own reader. kiwix-serve is not used and is never a source kind here. HONEST LIMIT, READ THIS BEFORE PROMISING ANYONE A SPECIALIST BOT: the Kiwix library is broad but shallow. It will give an astronomy bot Wikipedia, a Q&A archive, and a star catalog; it will not give it the observing handbooks, the current ephemerides, the instrument manuals, or the journal literature a real enthusiast wants. That gap is exactly why 'corpus' and 'docs' rows exist, and it is also why this list is short: most of what would close the gap is copyrighted and cannot be redistributed, and we would rather ship a small honest list than a long list we cannot license. Say the gap out loud to the owner; do not paper over it.
